Mike Tuhill will confirm with the Agricultural Commission and the town manager/town counsel before the planning board formally votes to add an Agricultural Commission seat to the Open Space Committee.

meetings.summary: The Lunenburg Planning Board endorsed a routine ANR lot-line adjustment for a Unitil substation expansion, then continued a contested storm water permit for 255 Sunny Hill Road to November 10 after abutters raised unresolved drainage-pipe and lawsuit concerns and outstanding taxes on the property surfaced. The board then closed public hearings and voted to recommend to town meeting both an MBTA Communities compliance bylaw (achieving compliance by raising the density cap at the existing Tritown development rather than opening new land) and a minor amendment removing a paving requirement from the common driveways bylaw, alongside routine committee reports and administrative votes.

The chair reported that Richard Harris is again being retained by the town as interim consultant/land use manager, after a prior gap caused by limits on his allowed hours, not any problem with the working relationship.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board voted 5-0 to approve a common-driveway special permit and a stormwater permit for 558 and 560 Goodridge Street, both with standard conditions.
The board voted 5-0 to remove the Finance Committee, Parks Commission and at-large seats from the Master Plan Steering Committee.
The board approved a stormwater permit for 255 Sunny Hill Road, conditioned on the town's engineering consultant being satisfied with the responses.
Members did not resolve a dispute over a request to submit warrant motions on the ADU bylaw by the end of the week; feedback goes to the land use director within a week.
The board continued the 494 Electric Avenue hearing to February 10 and will wait for other boards' input before taking a position on 100 Townsend Harbor Road.

why_it_matters: The ADU and floodplain bylaw changes are state-mandated and are headed for a town meeting warrant, so the timing dispute bears on how much review residents' boards get before a vote they may be asked to take.
The Master Plan Steering Committee now has no seat for the Finance Committee or Parks Commission, which changes whose input shapes a plan that guides later budget and land-use decisions.
watch_next: February 10: the 494 Electric Avenue hearing resumes at 6:05 p.m., and a DCR representative may speak on the floodplain bylaw.
The draft ADU bylaw, due at the next meeting after members send feedback within a week.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board approved stormwater permits for 791 and 795 Lemonster Road and 70 Kilburn Street after closing each public hearing.
It approved the stormwater permit and a common-driveway special permit for 171 Arbor Street, with a condition that a shared-maintenance framework be recorded on the deeds.
It approved a modification to the site plan and special permit for a shed at 230 Flat Hill Road.
It required a peer review deposit from the applicant at 255 Sunny Hill Road, then continued that hearing and two others (494 Electric Ave, 558/560 Goodrich Street) to January 27.
The chair will put Master Plan Steering Committee membership on the next agenda and consult the Town Clerk on quorum.

why_it_matters: Stormwater permits and peer review rules decide who pays to manage drainage: members said the town budget has no money for peer review, so applicants fund it, and a drainage failure can fall on abutting homeowners.
Conditions recorded on deeds, such as maintenance duties for shared driveways and drainage, pass to later owners of those properties.
The Master Plan Steering Committee's quorum problem could affect when the town's long-range planning work can proceed.
